name: Isolated Absence of Upper Arm and Forearm with Hand Present
aliases: Isolated Upper Limb Agenesis with Hand Preservation
Congenital Absence of Humerus and Radius with Hand Present

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Upper Limb Agenesis

criteria.description: Congenital absence of the humerus and forearm bones with preservation of the hand
Presence of anatomically normal hand distal to absent upper arm and forearm
No evidence of systemic or syndromic abnormalities on clinical and genetic evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital absence of humerus and forearm bones with a preserved normal hand and exclusion of syndromic or systemic conditions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may be used to exclude syndromic causes.

rare.symptomName: Congenital malformation of the great arteries

imaging: Radiographs showing absence of humerus and forearm bones with preserved hand bones
MRI to assess soft tissue and muscle hypoplasia
genetic: Genetic testing to exclude syndromic causes such as Holt-Oram syndrome or other limb malformation syndromes
other: Clinical examination confirming normal hand anatomy distal to absent segments
Functional assessment of hand and residual limb mobility

distinguishingFeatures: Complete absence of entire limb including hand
Often associated with other systemic anomalies
Presence of hand or foot attached close to trunk with absent or hypoplastic intermediate limb segments
Usually involves multiple limbs and syndromic features
Hypoplasia or absence of radius with variable hand anomalies
Often associated with cardiac or hematological abnormalities

redFlags: Presence of systemic or syndromic abnormalities
Progressive neurological deficits in affected limb
Vascular compromise or ischemic changes in residual limb
references: Orphanet: Isolated Absence of Upper Arm and Forearm with Hand Present, ORPHA:294975
